wifi.title: Set WiFi Credentials
wifi.hostname_help: This will be used to display the name of this device on your network. It will also influence how the internal WiFi network will be called.

general.title: General Settings
general.heating_values: Enable processing and transmission of heating values
general.water_values: Enable processing and transmission of water values
general.aux_values: Enable processing and transmission of external temperature sensors
general.own_outside: Use your own outside temperature reference instead of that of the heating.
general.unknown_time: Use minimum safe heating when no clock is available
general.debug: Enable debug messages on the consoles
general.sniffing: Output received CAN messages on consoles.

leds.title: LED Configuration
leds.intro: Here you can specify GPIOs for signalling. These are designed to be used as LED outputs and are not driven by a PWM signal. Be aware though, that some of them switch on and off depending on status and may even show a pattern. Refer to the description below the fields for more info.
leds.status_help: The status LED will show the overall status of the device. It will show a heartbeat pattern, when the main application routine is working as expected.
leds.wifi_help: The Wi-Fi LED will show you if the device is connected to wireless lan.
leds.mqtt_help: The MQTT LED will not only show you if the device is connected to a MQTT broker but also activity when a message is sent or received.
leds.heating_help: The heating LED follows the burner's flame state. It blinks instead when CAN transmission errors are detected.

sensors.title: Auxiliary Sensors Configuration
sensors.label: Sensor Label
sensors.instructions: Enter a name (label) for the sensor and enter its address into the fields. The format of the address is
sensors.format_help: which is the same format used by the library to report addresses.
sensors.scan_help: on how to scan for addresses.

can.title: CAN-Bus Configuration
can.frequency_help: Enter the frequency of the quartz (oscillator) which is used by your CAN-Module. Usually it's 8MHz or 16MHz in some rare cases, though, 16MHz has been found to be more stable but your mileage may vary.
can.hex_help: Addresses have to be entered in their hexadecimal text representation.
can.sniff_help: You will find these addresses in the console output, when 'Sniffing' is enabled.

mqtt.prefix_help: Must match the MQTT discovery prefix configured in Home Assistant.
mqtt.device_help: Use a unique value for every controller on the MQTT broker. Changing it replaces the controller's discovered device.
mqtt.off_delay_help: Seconds before an active binary sensor resets; use 0 to disable.

mqtt_help.status: This topic is used for publishing general heating status like error code and flame status.
mqtt_help.status_request: Topic subscribed for triggering a status update on other topics
mqtt_help.heating_parameters: Topic subscribed for setting heating parameters
mqtt_help.heating_values: Topic for publishing heating values like feed temperature
mqtt_help.water_parameters: Topic subscribed for setting water parameters
mqtt_help.water_values: Topic for publishing water related values and temperatures
mqtt_help.auxiliary: Topic where temperature readings of externally connected sensors are published
mqtt_help.boost: Topic to activate the boost feature
mqtt_help.fast_heatup: Topic to activate the fast heatup feature

general_help.bus_timeout: Time in seconds before control over the heating is assumed when no other controllers have been detected on the bus.
general_help.posix: POSIX rule used locally without internet, for example CET-1CEST,M3.5.0,M10.5.0/3.
general_help.failsafe: Used when no valid heating command has been received within the timeout. A fresh command is required to leave fail-safe mode.
general_help.outside_override: This will use the value from 'AuxiliaryTemperature' found on the heating parameters topic instead of the readings from the thermistor that may or may not be attached to your heating.
